title: Epochal Minima: ingress/egress usage synthesis and sessionized minimums pilot
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Current hosted pricing pilots split billing into directional token meters (ingress vs egress) and session or per-request minima. Historically we've applied minima at the API key or session level with a fixed window and struggled to reconcile enterprise contract language in Security Questionnaires (SQs) that ask for predictable per-session floors and fair streaming handling. Goal: design and pilot a 'epochal minima' billing primitive that synthesizes ingress+egress into a single, time-epoch based usage signal, enabling sessionized minima that are both more predictable for customers and simpler to represent in enterprise SQs.
rationale: Problems we want to solve: (1) Customers with highly asymmetric input/output patterns find directional minima confusing and see unexpected bills; (2) Streaming sessions with large continuous token egress spikes penalize short-input-heavy customers; (3) Sales/legal need a clear, auditable mapping to SQ clauses about minimums and burst credits. By synthesizing usage into epoch buckets and computing a normalized 'usage score' (weighted ingress+egress) we can offer symmetric minima tiers that behave intuitively across conversational and batch workloads and can be documented in contract language.
proposal: Pilot variants: A) Epochal-sum baseline: compute every 1h epoch: cost_tokens = ingress_weight * ingress + egress_weight * egress; apply hourly minima per API key; B) Sessionized epoch: detect session_id or inactivity gap (5m default), aggregate epochs inside session and apply session-floor with decay window; C) Hybrid grace band: same as B but allow 72h rolling grace credits that offset shortfalls. Ingress/Egress weights: start with ingress_weight=0.6, egress_weight=1.0 (reflecting average cost delta), run sensitivity sims. Implementation notes: server will tag epochs at the redwood-ingress-epoch header, billing pipeline computes epoched aggregates (BigQuery), console will show epoch-level breakdowns. Provide an opt-in flag per org for 6-week trial.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: BigQuery query for epoch-level aggregates returns expected distributions for at least 100 pilot orgs
Billing: invoices show epochal minima line items that reconcile to raw token totals within 0.1% for sample customers
Customer messaging: docs + SQ language drafted and approved by legal that maps epochal minima to contract clauses
Behavior: no >5% unexpected increase in invoices for customers with >90th percentile egress-heavy workloads compared to control group
Observability: Console dashboard surfaces epoch breakdown, session counts, and grace credit utilization
Rollback: feature flag ready and QA tests for immediate disable without invoice corruption
experiment_design: Randomized opt-in A/B across orgs. 1:1 control vs experiment stratified by historical ingress/egress ratio buckets and ARR bands. Minimum sample: 200 orgs per arm or 30M tokens per arm. Monitoring windows: daily revenue delta, weekly churn signals, support cases tagged 'billing-epochal', and SQ acceptance for enterprise contracts.
measurement_metrics: Primary: net revenue delta attributed to minima change. Secondary: change in per-session median bill, number of support escalations, legal/SQ approval rate for contracts referencing minima. Signal queries: BigQuery job IDs will be added to attachments.
operational_steps: 1) Implement epoch tag + aggregation in serving runtime (ENG change). 2) Billing pipeline change to compute epoch minima on nightly billing job. 3) Console: epoch breakdown and opt-in toggle. 4) Legal: publish SQ wording and playbook for sales. 5) Run 6-week pilot with rollback criteria. 6) Postmortem + decision: scale, revise weights, or abandon.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: customers with unusual burst patterns may see invoice surprises -> Mitigation: initial opt-in + pre-bill preview for first 3 invoices; Risk: legal SQ language rejected -> Mitigation: include examples and audit trail logs; Risk: telemetry mismatch between serving and billing -> Mitigation: implement parity tests and ‘recompute’ job for comparison.

notes: Design decision: Use weighted synthesis instead of max(ingress,egress) to better reflect cost contributions from input preprocessing and output decoding.
SQ mapping: We will supply a one-page appendix that maps epochal minima to 'minimum purchase' contract language and provides two worked examples (chat-heavy app, embedding-heavy app).
Future: If pilot looks good, consider exposing custom epoch lengths for enterprise customers (e.g., 15m for real-time apps).
